text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Centre-right coalition tries to rally voters for Sunday's second round parliamentary election runoff.

-- Air France posts a 394 million franc profit for year to March 31, 1997, its first profit since 1989. The impact of its merger with former Air Inter on the accounts was not published. Chairman Christian Blanc calls for a privatisation.

-- Eurotunnel expects first net profits by year 2005, provided its financial restructuring plan is accepted by shareholders and bankers' pool. Expects a 2.83 billion franc loss for 1997, from 6 billion in 1996.
-- Government places formal offer of 13 Rafale aircraft with Dassault Aviation.
-- Computer services firm Cap Gemini expects strong turnover growth in 1997, to 18 billion francs.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Parliamentary election campaign turns into a duel between National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin and socialist party leader Lionel Jospin.
-- Investigation looks at alleged bribery at SNCF railway authority linked to the building of TGV high-speed train infrastructure.
-- Germany's Vega to buy a 20 percent stake in Bouygues-Stet Telecom.

-- Market operators surveyed on the various candidates said about Lionel Jospin "we don't have anything against him personnally", about Philippe Seguin "the least good choice on the right", about Alain Madelin "we've stopped dreaming of him so much," about Edouard Balladur "opinions are mixed," about Nicolas Sarkozy "the best of the Balladur supporters."
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Air France posts first profit since 1989.
LIBERATION
-- State to buy a 24.5 percent stake in businessman Francois Pinault's holding Artemis, which controls Pinault Printemps Redoute retail group.

-- Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin, likely prime minister should the left win Sunday's vote, would probably choose Dominique Strauss-Kahn as finance minister, Pierre Moscovici or Francois Hollande as budget minister, Martine Aubry as labour minister, Jean-Pierre Chevenement or Pierre Joxe as Justice Minister and Jacques Delors, Michel Rocard, Laurent Fabius or Jack Lang as foreign minister. Paul Quiles or Bertrand Delanoe were likely candidates for defence minister.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- LVMH luxury goods group signal will to battle Guinness, press ahead with plan to buy Guinness's stakes in LVMH beverages units, as it would raise shareholder value.
